title: Strings
game_role: When the game starts, Piko introduces himself with the sentence you wrote.
objective: Join, slice and format strings with f-strings
story: The village is full of signs, conversations and letters. In games, characters talk and names glow on the screen too. Today we play with text, that is, with **strings**!

sections.title: What is a string?
sections.body:
A string is a sequence of characters inside quotes. Single or double quotes both work: `'Piko'` or `"Piko"`.

- Join with `+`: `"Pi" + "ko"` gives `"Piko"`
- Repeat with `*`: `"ha" * 3` gives `"hahaha"`
- Measure with `len()`: `len("Piko")` gives `4`

sections.title: Reaching single letters
sections.body:
Every letter has a position number (an index), and counting **starts at 0**.

```python
word = "Python"
print(word[0])    # P
print(word[-1])   # n (first from the end)
print(word[0:3])  # Pyt (0, 1 and 2)
print(word[::-1]) # nohtyP (reversed)
```

sections.title: String methods
sections.body:
- `upper()` ALL CAPS, `lower()` all lowercase
- `title()` Capitalizes Each Word
- `replace("a", "e")` swaps letters
- `strip()` removes spaces at the start and end
- `count("a")` counts how many there are

sections.title: f-strings: put variables inside text
sections.body:
In text that starts with `f`, variables inside curly braces are replaced with their values:

```python
name = "Piko"
level = 3
print(f"{name} reached level {level}!")
```

This is the easiest way to write messages in games.

sections.title: Is it inside?
sections.body:
With `in` you can check whether a piece of text is inside another: `"ko" in "Piko"` gives `True`.

You ask whether two things are the same with `==`: `"map" == "map"` gives `True`.

examples.title: Join and repeat
examples.code:
first = "Pi"
second = "ko"
print(first + second)
print("ha" * 3)
print(len("Piko's Adventure"))

examples.title: f-string
examples.code:
name = "Piko"
gold = 42
print(f"{name} carries {gold} gold coins.")
print(f"{name.upper()} is coming!")

tasks.title: Signboard
tasks.prompt: Turn the text in `word` into capital letters, add `!` to the end and store it in `shout`. The result should be `PYTHON!`.
tasks.starter:
word = "python"

shout = ""  # word in capitals + "!"
print(shout)
hints: + "!" adds an exclamation mark to the end.

tasks.title: First and last letter
tasks.prompt: Put the first letter of `name` into `first` and the last letter into `last`. Use a negative index for the last letter.
tasks.solution:
name = "Piko"

first = name[0]
last = name[-1]
print(first, last)

tasks.title: Level message
tasks.prompt: Create the `message` variable with an f-string. The result should be exactly `Mia reached level 7!`, but the name and the number must come from the variables.
tasks.solution:
name = "Mia"
level = 7

message = f"{name} reached level {level}!"
print(message)
hints: An f-string starts with f: f"..."
Put the variables in curly braces: {name}

visual_task.title: Piko in the castle
visual_task.prompt:
Let's put Piko in a room surrounded by walls. `gap` is the number of empty squares on each side of Piko.

- `wall`: repeat `"#"` `gap * 2 + 3` times
- `room`: `"#"` + `gap` spaces + `"*"` + `gap` spaces + `"#"`
- Then print `wall`, `room`, `wall`.

With `gap = 3` the room should grow by itself.
visual_task.solution:
gap = 2
wall = "#" * (gap * 2 + 3)
room = "#" + " " * gap + "*" + " " * gap + "#"

print(wall)
print(room)
print(wall)
hints: A space is text too: " " * gap

challenge.title: Palindrome hunter
challenge.prompt: Words that read the same backwards are called palindromes: level, kayak, racecar. If `word` is a palindrome, `is_palindrome` should be `True`, otherwise `False`. No typing `True`; find it by comparing!
hints: Are two things the same? Ask with ==.

project_task.title: Character dialogue
project_task.prompt:
At the start of the game the hero introduces himself.

- First print a line of 30 `=` signs
- Then create `intro` with an f-string: `I'm Piko, the adventure begins!` (use `player_name` instead of Piko)
- Print `intro`
project_task.starter:
player_name = "Piko"

# 1) Print a line of 30 "=" signs

# 2) Create the intro sentence with an f-string
intro = ""
print(intro)
project_task.solution:
player_name = "Piko"

print("=" * 30)

intro = f"I'm {player_name}, the adventure begins!"
print(intro)
